intro.en: Wisp lost six lanterns, and the whole office is on the case. This is the large-office Halloween event edition: every team in the office plays the same six stops and six puzzles across Halloween weekend, October 30 to November 1, 2026, with a hint ladder at every stop (three hints, the third is the Ranger assist) and the organizer guide's scoring and tiebreakers deciding the standings. Pick each team's Dial level — Cozy, Spooky, After Dark, or full Overdrive — and bring all six lights home for the lantern parade finale.

outro.en: All six lanterns are lit, and the parade is marching for the whole office. Gather every team, take the group photo, and show this screen at the finale table — the office brought every last lantern home.

stops.name: The Welcome Pumpkin

story.cozy: Wisp's lanterns bounced out of her basket when Dr. Z's experimental wind-up machine went BZZT. The first one rolled right to this pumpkin. Can your team help her gather all six?
story.spooky: The pumpkin's grin flickers though no flame is inside it. From somewhere behind the carved eyes comes the slow click of a winding key. When it stops, a second click answers from the dark. The first lantern is glowing inside.
story.afterdark: FIELD RECORD 01 — 00:13. The first lantern is inside the pumpkin. The recording captures a winding key turning by itself, then a second mechanism answering from beyond the path. Dr. Z's notes say the machine cannot operate without its operator. His signature appears on the next page—in fresh ink.
story.overdrive: DR. Z'S OFFICIAL INCIDENT REPORT: My machine made one tiny puff of wind. SIX lanterns escaped. This pumpkin has the first. Retrieve it before Wisp files a complaint—and before I have to apologize.

stops.wisp: That's MINE! Oh — oh! It still remembers me. Quick, light it!
stops.lit: One down! See how it glows? That's my happy leaking out.

cozy.q: Count the pumpkins in the patch picture your organizer showed you. How many are smiling?

spooky.q: The carved pumpkins are watching the street. How many are smiling in the patch?

afterdark.q: A lantern's glow reveals the smiling pumpkins. How many smiling pumpkins are there?

overdrive.q: Dr. Z demands a quick count: how many pumpkins are smiling?

fallback.q: What color is the ribbon on the welcome sign?

cozy: Look low — lanterns love the ground.
Count slowly, out loud, as a team.
Ranger assist: the smiling pumpkins are 4.
spooky: Look low — lanterns love the ground.
Count slowly, out loud, as a team.
Ranger assist: the smiling pumpkins are 4.
afterdark: Look low — lanterns love the ground.
Count slowly, out loud, as a team.
Ranger assist: the smiling pumpkins are 4.
overdrive: Look low — lanterns love the ground.
Count slowly, out loud, as a team.
Ranger assist: the smiling pumpkins are 4.

stops.name: The Whispering Oak

story.cozy: Oakie the oak caught a scrap of Dr. Z's map in his branches. Wisp thinks it points to the next lantern. Ask the tree nicely—he likes good listeners.
story.spooky: Oakie's branches scrape together overhead. A map is pinned to the bark, though nobody saw it arrive. One route is crossed out so violently the paper has torn. Beneath it, in handwriting that looks almost like yours: DON'T FOLLOW THE LIGHT THAT MOVES.
story.afterdark: FIELD RECORD 02 — The map was dry when found, but the bark beneath it is wet with cold condensation. One route has been scratched away. On the reverse, a message has appeared in your team's handwriting: DON'T FOLLOW THE LIGHT THAT MOVES. No one admits writing it.
story.overdrive: Oakie intercepted Dr. Z's map and is now acting like head of security. Get the next clue from the tree, Keepers. Yes, I know trees don't talk. This one has standards.

stops.wisp: Shhh — Oakie is sleeping. He only hides things for friends. We're friends, right?
stops.lit: Got it! Oakie says you're officially tree-approved.

cozy.q: Find the oak. How many wooden swings or benches face it?

spooky.q: Riddle: I have arms but cannot hug, I wear a coat but cannot feel cold. The wind whispers through me but I never speak. What am I?

afterdark.q: The oak was planted in 1824. How many decades has it stood? (Round to nearest whole decade)

overdrive.q: Dr. Z's challenge: The oak's canopy spans 15m. If each lantern hangs 3m apart, how many lanterns fit in a straight line across the canopy?

fallback.q: What is carved on the small sign by the oak?

cozy: Face the tree like it is facing you.
Only count the ones looking at the oak.
spooky: Its arms are branches and its coat is bark.
It stands in the ground and never moves.
Ranger assist: it is the tree.
afterdark: Subtract 1824 from this year, then divide by ten.
overdrive: Divide the canopy span by the spacing.

stops.name: The Giggling Graveyard (pretend!)

story.cozy: The pretend graveyard is Dr. Z's decoy—foam stones, silly epitaphs, and ghostly giggles recorded on his machine. Wisp says the real lantern is nearby. Don't let the joke distract you!
story.spooky: The foam stones are harmless. The laughter is not. It plays from a speaker under the nearest stone, then cuts off when you approach. In the sudden silence, something beneath the prop taps three times—waits—and taps once more.
story.afterdark: FIELD RECORD 03 — The graveyard is a staged set. The tapping is not part of the sound file; the recording's waveform is silent during it. Four knocks, always. The final frame shows a shadow standing behind the team. Reviewers confirm nobody was standing there when the clip was made.
story.overdrive: You have defeated Dr. Z's terrifying graveyard of FOAM. His spooky sound effect is stuck on loop. Laugh at the villain later; find the lantern now!

stops.wisp: Tag, you're it! Kidding — unless…? No, kidding. Probably.
stops.lit: The ghosts are doing the wave. That's their applause. You're welcome.

cozy.q: One foam tombstone says R.I.P. — Rest In... what? (The silly word on the stone!)

spooky.q: Riddle: I have a head and a tail but no body. I lie in the dark waiting. What am I?

afterdark.q: The 1918 flu pandemic killed 675,000 Americans. If this graveyard represents 1/1000th of that, how many 'souls' are here?

overdrive.q: Dr. Z's challenge: The ghosts giggle every 7 seconds. How many giggles in one minute? (Round to nearest whole number)

fallback.q: How many foam tombstones are there?

cozy: Read the stones — one of them is joking.
It rhymes with the patch from Stop 1.
spooky: Ranger assist: it is a coin.
overdrive: Sixty seconds in a minute, one giggle every seven.

stops.name: The Spider's Counting Web

story.cozy: Mrs. Spider found a glowing thread snagged on Dr. Z's decoy. It leads toward the next lantern. She'll help untangle the clue—eight legs are better than two!
story.spooky: A silver thread stretches across the web, trembling without wind. At its center hangs a tiny metal tag stamped with Dr. Z's crooked Z. The web tightens, strand by strand, around something unseen. From the dark comes a dry whisper: 'You took the wrong one.'
story.afterdark: FIELD RECORD 04 — The tag matches the mark on Dr. Z's machine. The thread runs toward the next lantern, but its shadow points the opposite way. A voice on the recorder says, 'You took the wrong one.' The recorder was switched off when the voice was captured.
story.overdrive: Mrs. Spider has trapped a piece of my very expensive lantern rig. I would like it back. She would like you to solve the clue first. Frankly, I'm afraid to negotiate with her.

stops.wisp: Mrs. Spider says hi. She says it with all eight legs. It's a lot of hi.
stops.lit: Untangled! Mrs. Spider is doing a happy leg-dance. All eight. It's a LOT.

cozy.q: A real spider has 8 legs. Mrs. Spider is holding up 3 legs to wave. How many legs are on the ground?

spooky.q: Riddle: I weave without a loom, I trap without a cage. My silk is stronger than steel by weight. What am I?

afterdark.q: Orb weavers rebuild their web every night. If Mrs. Spider has been here 11 years, approximately how many webs has she built? (Ignore leap years)

overdrive.q: Dr. Z's challenge: A spider web has 20 radial threads. If each radial thread takes 2 minutes to spin, how long does the full web take?

cozy: Start with 8 legs, like every spider.
spooky: She has eight legs and builds the web herself.
Ranger assist: it is the spider.
afterdark: One web a night, 365 nights a year.
overdrive: Multiply the threads by the minutes each.

stops.name: The Owl's Night Watch

story.cozy: Professor Hoot has Dr. Z's final note. The last lantern is waiting at the parade ground, but it needs all six lights to make the parade shine. You're nearly there!
story.spooky: Professor Hoot will not look at the path behind you. His note says the final lantern waits at the parade ground. Beneath that, in smaller letters: SIX LIGHTS MAKE A PATH. SEVEN MAKE A WAY BACK. The owl folds his wings and refuses to explain.
story.afterdark: FIELD RECORD 05 — Professor Hoot's note lists six lanterns, then a seventh line crossed out so hard the paper has split. The final instruction is clear: reunite the lights at the parade ground. The margin contains one last warning: IF YOU HEAR YOUR TEAM COUNTING, CHECK THAT EVERYONE IS HERE.
story.overdrive: Professor Hoot has my final note and is grading my handwriting. Focus, Keepers: one stop left. Bring the lights together, save the parade, and please do not let the owl review my entire notebook.

stops.wisp: Professor Hoot is very serious. Do your serious face. …Not that serious. Dial it back.
stops.lit: ‘Hoo,’ he says. That's owl for ‘well done.’ I translated. You're welcome.

cozy.q: Professor Hoot guards this stop's lantern. What kind of bird is he?

spooky.q: Riddle: I fly without wings, I see without eyes. I turn my head almost all the way around. What am I?

afterdark.q: Barred owls live about 10 years in the wild. If Professor Hoot is 7, how many years does he likely have left?

overdrive.q: Dr. Z's challenge: An owl can rotate its head 270 degrees. How many more degrees would it need for a full 360?

fallback.q: What two letters does an owl 'say'?

cozy: Look at the sign art — he's watching you.
Twilight is this bird's favorite time.
spooky: It hoots and turns its head almost all the way around.
afterdark: Ten years of life minus seven lived.

stops.name: The Lantern Parade Ground

story.cozy: The last lantern! Bring its light together with the others and Wisp's parade can begin. Dr. Z's machine is quiet at last—and there's room in the parade for one reformed mad scientist.
story.spooky: Six lanterns burn across the parade ground. Their shadows stretch toward the team, not away from the light. A seventh shadow lifts its hand. Dr. Z steps out beside his silent machine—but the shadow keeps waving after he stops. Then the lanterns flare, and every shadow turns toward the road home.
story.afterdark: FIELD RECORD 06 — All six lanterns recovered. Dr. Z's machine is silent. The seventh shadow remains after its owner leaves the frame. At 00:13, the lights go out for one second; when they return, the shadow is gone and the road home is visible. Final note: the experiment ended. The recording did not.
story.overdrive: FINAL LANTERN RECOVERED! The machine is off, the parade is ON, and Dr. Z has been assigned one job: carry the snacks. You saved the night, Keepers. I am absolutely not getting sentimental about this.

stops.wisp: This is it — the last one! My hands are all shaky. Do I have hands? I'm shaky anyway!
stops.lit: IT'S LIT! Look at them all — look at ME! I'm basically a sunrise!

cozy.q: Teamwork finale: how many lanterns did you light on the whole hunt (including this one)?

spooky.q: Riddle: I am born in fire, I die in water, and I glow in the dark. What am I?

afterdark.q: The first lantern festival was in China over 1800 years ago. Approximately how many centuries ago was that?

overdrive.q: Dr. Z's final challenge: If your team lit 6 lanterns in 45 minutes, what was your average time per lantern?

fallback.q: Say the magic words out loud as a team: 'Light the way, Wisp!' then type: wisp

cozy: Count the stops on your map.
spooky: You light it when the power goes out.
Ranger assist: it is a candle.
afterdark: A century is one hundred years.
overdrive: Divide the minutes by the lanterns.
